newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia to start EU ratification procedure.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia to start EU ratification procedure.

text.p: Slovenian Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek said on Wednesday the government would start procedures on Thursday for ratifying an association agreement with the European Union.

"The government will debate a law on ratification of the EU agreement tomorrow which it is also expected to send to parliament," Drnovsek told reporters. Parliament was expected to ratify the agreement in May, he added.
The accord -- a trade and cooperation pact that carries with it a promise of eventual EU membership -- was signed in June last year but has yet to be ratified by most EU parliaments.
Slovenia hopes to become a full EU member as soon as possible.
Drnovsek said his centre-left Liberal Democrats would push for legislation changes in line with the association accord to start immediately after other countries had ratified the deal.
Last year Slovenia agreed to change its constitution to allow foreigners to own real estate in the country within four years of the association agreement taking effect.

"It is our (the Liberal Democrats') stand that the constitution should be changed as soon as it becomes clear that the changes will be supported by a two-third majority (in parliament)," Drnovsek said.
According to Slovenian legislation any constitutional change needs to be supported by at least two thirds of parliamentary members.

Slovenia is so far the only one of the successor states of the former Yugoslavia to have signed the association agreement, while nine other ex-communist states -- Poland, Hungary, the Czech Republic, Slovakia, Estonia, Lithuania, Latvia, Romania and Bulgaria -- have signed similar agreements.
